prompt: Turn this flat diagram into a photograph of the floor of an old, dark pine forest under a dense canopy, four metres across. Keep the composition exactly: every shape stays where it is, at the same size and in the same colour family. The fine strokes become fallen rust-brown and grey-brown pine needles lying criss-cross in a thick, even mat, and the darker background becomes damp needle litter and black humus between them. Only needles: no moss, no plants, no seedlings, no leaves, no twigs, no cones and no stones. The mat is the same everywhere in the frame, with no centre and no larger shapes. Shot straight down from directly above as a flat orthographic photograph: flat overcast diffuse daylight, no cast shadows, no specular highlights, uniform exposure from edge to edge, no horizon, no perspective, no vignette, sharp focus everywhere. Photorealistic, high detail, natural muted colours of a cold, damp late-autumn borderland.
